name: Maximum-Generated Nested-Section Substitution
statement: For a nonempty proper test and nonempty distinct outer sections, a maximum-generated substituted class can occur only if both inputs are maximum-generated. Conversely, if both inputs are maximum-generated and the two outer sections are nested, then the substituted class is maximum-generated. The converse also holds for a downset test, or a coordinate reflection of one, by rank-preserving filtering.
proof: Sections of the output recover the outer class and the test or its complement, proving necessity. For nested shores $S\subseteq B$, standardize a parent of the outer expansion to consecutive nested maximum shores with marked sections $B,S$. Raise a parent of the test to a consecutive pair whose marked sections are the full test cube and the test. Extend both pairs to maximum sequences, delay their upper levels, and take the level sum at one below the sum rank. Its marked section is $(B\times T)\cup(S\times\{0,1\}^Y)$. Downset tests follow from the database's rank-preserving filter theorem.
